chunks.text:
## What Delay Repay covers

Delay Repay compensates you when you arrive at your destination later than
scheduled, regardless of the cause of the delay. You do not need to show that
the operator was at fault.

Compensation is based on the **delay to your arrival** at your final
destination, not on the departure delay.

## Compensation bands

| Delay on arrival | Compensation | Calculated on |
|---|---|---|
| 15 to 29 minutes | **25%** | single fare paid |
| 30 to 59 minutes | **50%** | single fare paid |
| 60 to 119 minutes | **100%** | single fare paid |
| 120 minutes or more | **100%** | total fare paid, including the return leg |

Delays of **under 15 minutes do not qualify** for compensation.

## How the amount is calculated

Compensation is always calculated on the fare **you actually paid**, after any
railcard discount. It is not calculated on the undiscounted fare.

Worked example: a journey booked at an Off-Peak fare of 45.00 GBP with a
one-third railcard discount costs 29.97 GBP. If that journey arrives 47 minutes
late, it falls in the 30 to 59 minute band, so compensation is 50% of 29.97 GBP,
which is **14.99 GBP**.

## Claiming

- Claims must be submitted within **28 days** of the delayed journey.
- You need your booking reference and the date of travel.
- One claim per booking reference per journey. A booking already claimed against
  cannot be claimed again.
- Compensation is paid by the original payment method by default. Bank transfer
  and rail vouchers are also available.
- Claims are normally processed within 10 working days.

## Cancellations

If your booked service is **cancelled** and you choose not to travel, you are
entitled to a **full refund** rather than Delay Repay, and no administration fee
applies regardless of fare type, including Advance.

If your service is cancelled and you do travel on a later service, Delay Repay
applies in the normal way based on how late you arrive at your destination.

## Frequently asked

**Can I claim Delay Repay on an Advance ticket?**
Yes. Delay Repay applies to all fare types, including non-refundable Advance
fares.

**My train was cancelled and I travelled an hour later. What do I get?**
Compensation is based on your actual arrival delay. If you arrived 60 to 119
minutes late, that is 100% of the single fare paid.

**Does a missed connection count?**
Yes, provided the connection was part of the same booking and the delay to your
final arrival meets the 15-minute threshold.

**Can I claim twice for the same journey if both legs were late?**
No. Compensation is assessed once, on the delay to your final destination.

## Advance fares

Advance fares are the cheapest option and are released in limited quantities for
each individual service.

- **Valid only on the specific booked service.** If you miss your train, the
  ticket is not valid on a later one.
- **No changes permitted.** The booked service cannot be amended.
- **No refunds permitted.** The fare is non-refundable once purchased.
- Must be booked before the day of travel in most cases.
- Railcard discounts apply and are not time-restricted on Advance fares.

If your booked service is **cancelled or significantly delayed by the
operator**, the normal Advance restrictions are suspended. You may travel on an
alternative service at no extra cost, or claim a full refund with no
administration fee. This is an operator-caused exception and overrides the
no-change and no-refund rules above.

A delay counts as **significant** for this purpose at **60 minutes or more**. A
cancellation always counts, whatever the fare type. Shorter delays do not
suspend the fare restrictions, but may still qualify for Delay Repay once you
have travelled -- see `delay-repay.md`, where the threshold is 15 minutes.

## Off-Peak fares

Off-Peak fares offer moderate flexibility at a mid-range price.

- Valid on off-peak services only. See `ticket-validity.md` for peak definitions.
- **Changes are permitted**, subject to a **10 GBP administration fee** plus any
  difference in fare.
- **Refunds are permitted**, subject to the same **10 GBP administration fee**.
- Not valid on services departing within the morning or evening peak windows.

## Anytime fares

Anytime fares are the most expensive and the most flexible.

- Valid on **any** service on the date of travel.
- **Fully changeable with no fee.** Only a fare difference, if any, applies.
- **Fully refundable with no fee.**
- No time restrictions.

## Summary table

| Fare type | Refundable | Changeable | Admin fee | Tied to one service |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Advance | No | No | n/a | Yes |
| Off-Peak | Yes | Yes | 10 GBP | No |
| Anytime | Yes | Yes | None | No |

## Frequently asked

**Can I change an Advance ticket?**
No. Advance tickets are tied to a single booked service and cannot be changed or
refunded. The only exception is when the operator cancels or significantly
delays your booked service, in which case you may travel on an alternative
service or claim a full refund.

**What happens if I miss my Advance train?**
The ticket is no longer valid and a new ticket must be purchased. If the reason
you missed it was a delay on a connecting service covered by the same booking,
you are protected and should speak to staff.

**Is the administration fee charged per ticket or per booking?**
Per ticket.

**Can I upgrade from Standard to First after booking?**
On Off-Peak and Anytime fares, yes, subject to availability and the fare
difference. Advance fares cannot be upgraded; a new ticket must be purchased.

## Luggage allowance

- **Three items per passenger**: two large items plus one small item of hand
  luggage. There is no weight charge.
- Maximum size for a large item is 30 x 70 x 90 cm.
- You must be able to carry and stow your own luggage. Staff are not able to
  lift luggage for you.
- Luggage must be stowed in the racks provided, in the vestibule racks, or
  above or below your seat. It must not block aisles, doorways or wheelchair
  spaces.
- Excess luggage may be refused if the service is busy.

### Items needing extra arrangements

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Skis, surfboards, golf clubs | Carried free if stowed safely, subject to space |
| Musical instruments | Large instruments may need a seat reservation purchased for them |
| Pushchairs and prams | Carried free; must be folded if the vestibule is congested |
| Mobility scooters | Permitted up to 120 x 70 cm and 300 kg including occupant |

## Bicycles

- **Folding bicycles** travel free on all services at any time, with no
  reservation, provided they are folded.
- **Non-folding bicycles** require a **free cycle reservation**, booked in
  advance. Spaces are limited, typically two to four per train.
- Non-folding bicycles are **not permitted on weekday peak departures**
  (06:30 to 09:29 and 16:00 to 18:59, Monday to Friday) on long-distance
  services.
- Electric bicycles are treated as non-folding bicycles. E-scooters are not
  carried.
- A cycle reservation is tied to a specific service. If your service is
  cancelled, the reservation moves with ticket acceptance but space on the
  replacement service is not guaranteed.

## Accessible travel

### Wheelchair spaces

- Every long-distance service in this demo has **one or two dedicated wheelchair
  spaces** in Standard class, each with an adjacent companion seat.
- Wheelchair spaces are reserved, not first-come. Book the space at the same
  time as the ticket.
- The reserved space appears on the booking as a seat of type
  `wheelchair space`, for example coach B, space WC1.
- Maximum wheelchair dimensions for the onboard space are 70 cm wide by 120 cm
  long.

### Assisted travel

- Assistance can be booked up to **2 hours before departure**. Booking further
  ahead is recommended so that staff are rostered at both ends of the journey.
- Assistance covers help getting to the platform, **ramp assistance for boarding
  and alighting**, help finding the reserved space or seat, and help at
  interchange stations during a connection.
- Assistance is recorded against the booking. When a booking carries assistance,
  any change or rebooking must re-confirm it on the new service, because
  assistance follows the service and not the ticket.
- Turn up and go assistance is available without booking at staffed stations,
  but cannot be guaranteed.

### Disruption and assistance

- A traveller with booked assistance whose service is cancelled is rebooked onto
  the next service **with a confirmed wheelchair space**, not merely the next
  service. A service showing zero wheelchair spaces available is not a valid
  alternative even if ticket acceptance is in place.
- Assistance must be re-confirmed on the replacement service, including at any
  new interchange station.
- Where no accessible alternative is available on the day, accessible onward
  transport is arranged at no cost to the traveller.

### Other provisions

- **Assistance dogs** travel free, with no reservation and no muzzle
  requirement. Up to two per passenger.
- **Other dogs and small pets** travel free, up to two per passenger. Dogs must
  be on a lead or in a carrier, and must not occupy a seat.
- Accessible toilets are provided on all long-distance services in this demo.
- Priority seating near doorways is available on request to passengers who need
  it, regardless of reservation.

## Frequently asked

**Can I take a non-folding bike on the 07:15 from Euston?**
No. 07:15 is inside the weekday morning peak window, so non-folding bicycles are
not carried on that departure. A folding bicycle is fine.

**My service was cancelled and I use a wheelchair. Am I just put on the next
train?**
No. You are rebooked onto the next service that has a confirmed wheelchair
space, and your ramp assistance is re-confirmed for that service at both ends.

**Do I pay for a wheelchair space?**
No. The space itself carries no charge. You pay the normal fare for the
journey.

**How late can I book assistance?**
Up to 2 hours before departure, though earlier is better so staff can be
rostered at every station you pass through.

**Is there a charge for extra luggage?**
No, there is no weight or excess charge, but carriage is subject to space and
you must be able to handle your own bags.

## Discount

All railcards listed below give **one third off** eligible fares, applied at the
time of booking. The discount is calculated on the adult single fare before any
booking fee.

## Available railcards

### Two Together Railcard

- **Discount:** one third off for both travellers.
- **Eligibility:** two named adults, both named on the card.
- **Key condition:** both named cardholders **must travel together** on every
  journey where the discount is used.
- **Time restriction:** applies to **Off-Peak and Anytime fares only**, which
  cannot be discounted for departures before 09:30 Monday to Friday.
  **Advance fares are unrestricted** and may be discounted on any service.
- Valid for one year from purchase.

### 16-25 Railcard

- **Discount:** one third off.
- **Eligibility:** aged 16 to 25, or a mature student in full-time education.
- **Minimum fare:** a minimum fare applies to **Anytime** tickets for journeys
  departing before 10:00 Monday to Friday. The minimum fare does not apply to
  Advance or Off-Peak fares, nor at weekends or on public holidays.
- Valid for one or three years.

### Senior Railcard

- **Discount:** one third off.
- **Eligibility:** aged 60 or over.
- **Time restriction:** no discount on Anytime fares before 09:30 Monday to
  Friday.

### Disabled Persons Railcard

- **Discount:** one third off for the cardholder and one adult companion.
- **Eligibility:** holders who meet the published disability criteria.
- **Time restriction:** none. The discount applies at all times, including the
  morning peak.

## Frequently asked

**Does my railcard discount apply to Advance fares?**
Yes. Advance fares can be discounted with any of the railcards above, and the
morning time restrictions do not apply to Advance fares.

**What happens if I travel without the railcard I booked with?**
The discounted ticket is not valid. You may be asked to pay the full undiscounted
fare for your journey.

**Can two railcards be combined on one booking?**
No. Only one railcard discount may be applied per ticket.

**Does the Two Together discount still apply if only one of us travels?**
No. Both named cardholders must be present. If only one travels, the discounted
ticket is not valid.

**Is the discount applied to the Delay Repay compensation I receive?**
Compensation is calculated on the fare **you actually paid**, which is the
discounted amount. See `delay-repay.md`.

chunks.doc_title: Ticket Validity, Peak Times and Routing
chunks.text:
## Peak and off-peak windows

Peak restrictions are assessed on the **departure time of the first train of
your journey**, on Mondays to Fridays only.

| Window | Times | Applies |
|---|---|---|
| Morning peak | **06:30 to 09:29** | Monday to Friday |
| Off-peak (midday) | 09:30 to 15:59 | Monday to Friday |
| Evening peak | **16:00 to 18:59** | Monday to Friday |
| Off-peak (evening) | 19:00 to end of service | Monday to Friday |
| Off-peak (all day) | all services | Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays |

Off-Peak tickets are **not valid** for departures inside either peak window.
Anytime tickets are valid in all windows. Advance tickets are tied to one
specific booked service, so peak windows do not restrict them at all.

chunks.doc_title: Ticket Validity, Peak Times and Routing
chunks.section: How long a ticket is valid for
chunks.text:
## How long a ticket is valid for

| Fare type | Validity |
|---|---|
| Advance | The single booked service only. Not valid before or after it. |
| Off-Peak | Any off-peak service on the printed date of travel. |
| Anytime | Any service on the printed date of travel. |

A ticket remains valid for a journey that **starts** on the printed date, even
if it finishes after midnight. If you are already on board a service that
departed on the correct date, the ticket covers you to your destination.

chunks.doc_title: Ticket Validity, Peak Times and Routing
chunks.text:
## Railcard time restrictions

Railcard restrictions and peak restrictions are **separate rules** and both have
to be satisfied.

- Railcard discounts on **Advance** fares are never time-restricted.
- Railcard discounts on **Off-Peak and Anytime** fares may carry a restriction,
  typically before 09:30 Monday to Friday. The exact restriction depends on the
  railcard; see `railcards.md`.

This is why an early-morning Advance ticket can legitimately carry a railcard
discount even though the same railcard would be restricted on an Anytime ticket
at the same time of day.

chunks.doc_title: Ticket Validity, Peak Times and Routing
chunks.text:
## Routing

Tickets are issued against a **route**, not a specific set of trains.

- **Route: Any Permitted** allows any reasonable route between the origin and
  destination. Most tickets in this demo are Any Permitted.
- **Operator-specific** tickets are valid only on the named operator's services.
  An Advance fare is always effectively operator-specific, because it names one
  service.
- Breaking your journey (stopping off at an intermediate station and continuing
  later the same day) is permitted on Off-Peak and Anytime tickets, and is not
  permitted on Advance tickets.
- You may not travel beyond your destination, or start short of your origin in
  the direction of travel, unless the route permits it.

chunks.doc_title: Ticket Validity, Peak Times and Routing
chunks.text:
## Split ticketing

Buying two or more tickets covering consecutive parts of a journey is permitted,
and is sometimes cheaper than a single through ticket.

- The train **must call at the station where the tickets split**. It does not
  need to be a station where you get off.
- Each ticket must be valid in its own right, including any peak restriction at
  the time that leg departs.
- If a journey is split, Delay Repay is assessed against the delay to your
  **final arrival** across the whole journey, not per ticket. One claim covers
  the journey.
- A split involving an Advance leg means that leg is still tied to its booked
  service, so missing an earlier connection invalidates it.

chunks.doc_title: Ticket Validity, Peak Times and Routing
chunks.text:
## Reservations

- Advance tickets always include a seat reservation on the booked service.
- Off-Peak and Anytime tickets may include an optional reservation. The ticket
  stays valid if you travel on a different service; only the reservation is
  lost.
- During disruption, reservations on the affected service are released and seats
  become available to anyone holding a valid ticket.

chunks.doc_title: Ticket Validity, Peak Times and Routing
chunks.text:
## Frequently asked

**Is 09:30 peak or off-peak?**
Off-peak. The morning peak ends at 09:29, so a 09:30 departure is outside it.

**I have an Off-Peak ticket and the only train left is at 17:40 on a Tuesday.
Can I travel?**
No. 17:40 falls inside the evening peak, so an Off-Peak ticket is not valid. You
would need to pay the difference up to an Anytime fare, or travel after 19:00.

**Are peak restrictions based on departure or arrival?**
Departure, specifically the departure of the first train of your journey.

**Do peak restrictions apply at weekends?**
No. Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays are off-peak all day.

**Does ticket acceptance during disruption override peak restrictions?**
Yes. When ticket acceptance is in place because the operator cancelled or
severely delayed your service, you may travel on alternative services regardless
of the normal peak restriction on your ticket.
